# Added 'demo sort [name]' to print a deterministic Hogwarts house (commit de416f9)

Handoff from crew c1, in demo/house-sort, 2026-11-10 16:18.

## Done

- `sort.go`: `sortHouse(name)` hashes the trimmed, lower-cased name with sha256 and takes the first 4 bytes mod 4 to index the four houses.
- `main.go`: `run()` dispatches `sort [name]` (name from first arg or first line of stdin). No args still prints the existing greeting. `sort` with no name, or an unknown command, prints usage to stderr and exits 2.
- `sort_test.go`: determinism, a pinned value (Harry Potter -> Ravenclaw), normalisation, all outputs are one of the four houses, and CLI behaviour (arg, stdin, usage errors).
- `README.md`: usage and tests documented.
- Commit de416f9 on `house-sort`. No PR, since the demo repo has only a local origin.

## Learned

- Decisions d1-d3 are recorded on the mission.
- Stdin: with no argument, `sort` reads stdin. A terminal is detected and treated as "no name", so it prints usage instead of blocking. A non-terminal stdin that never closes (as in some harnesses) will block, which is normal Unix behaviour.
- `go run` reports exit 1 when the child exits 2. Check the real exit code with a built binary.

## Left

- Normalisation only trims and lower-cases, as the brief says. "Harry  Potter" (double space) gives a different house from "Harry Potter". Collapsing internal whitespace would be a one-line change if wanted, but it would change results, so I didn't do it unasked.
